status_note: Reproduces on 2.0.0 (Python wheel) on arm64 macOS; read in the source at v2.0.0. Not checked against the latest release or main, and the duckdb/duckdb issues were not searched.
title: `HUGEINT` to `DOUBLE` of a negative value rounds twice
summary: `CastBigintToFloating` (https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/v2.0.0/src/common/types/hugeint.cpp#L458-L469) computes a negative value as `-REAL_T(UINT64_MAX - lower) - 1`, which rounds twice in `REAL_T`, so the result can be one unit in the last place from the correctly rounded one. `BIGINT` to `DOUBLE` of the same value is correct.
It reaches `avg` of integers: the sum is a `HUGEINT`, and every path that casts it to `DOUBLE` inherits the error for a negative sum of magnitude 2^53 and above.
repro: `SELECT (-9007199254740994)::HUGEINT::DOUBLE, (-9007199254740994)::BIGINT::DOUBLE` gives `-9007199254740992.0` and `-9007199254740994.0`. The mean of one value shows it: `SELECT avg(v) FROM (SELECT -9007199254740994::BIGINT v)` gives `-9007199254740992.0`, grouped and ungrouped, where the value is a double.
handling: None needed in the SQL sverify writes (it casts the sum to `BIGINT` first, `dialect.py`, `int_avg`). The DuckDB profile's model of `avg` allows for it through the fact's bound (12d-2).
